habit_scope: When the house leaves the IRC R602.10 box. APA Table 23 / WFCM 3.4.4.2 / SDPWS. Not MF podium. Not Wasatch/Fontana habit. ALTERNATIVE_TO m-P08-bwl-wsp.
how_it_is_done: Use when the house leaves the IRC braced-wall box (spacing, openings, wind/SDC, or plan reviewer sends it). Permit gate is engineer. Not a multifamily podium shearwall.

Hold-downs usual to resist overturning (APA Fig 12). Do not copy the WFCM 160 mph / SDC D1 worked example (straps every stud, tight nailing, 16 in kept as practice) onto a low-wind IRC CS-WSP house (D5).

Edge nails 6 / 4 / 3 / 2 in as unit shear rises (APA Table 23). Fasteners 3/8 in from panel edges. Field typically 6 in on thinner panels at 24 in studs, otherwise 12 in. 3x framing (or two 2xs) at adjoining panel edges when edge nailing is 2 in, and in SDC D/E/F when shear exceeds the table trigger (APA Table 23 notes).

Glencoe §16.4 8d common or galv box @ 3 in OC to all studs, blocking, and sills is this engineered/high-hazard vocabulary — NOT BWL habit (D1). Prefab steel panel or moment frame per engineer (ch16) is CLASS/engineer, not a Method.

WFCM 3.4.4.2 names segmented / perforated shear walls with 3.5:1 aspect; the workbook 160-mph example uses 8d common 6/12 on 3/8 in WSP full height as its standard shear wall with max studs 16 in and min segment 2.6 ft. That example is high-hazard, not mild-climate habit. Interior 1/2 in GWB 5d cooler 7/10 in that example is not IRC BWL credit (D6 lives on the BWL method).

ABTG ABW: WSP edge nailing <=4 in OC plus hold-downs to a continuous foundation — engineered-adjacent, not Method WSP. FTAO is an engineering method (APA) for force around openings; PE tool, not habit.
Sheathing still 1/8 in gaps; do not glue unless AHJ allows high-seismic adhesive (APA). Strength axis either way except 3-ply plywood >16 in OC perpendicular (APA).
CS-PF portals stay on m-P08-bwl-wsp (IRC path without hold-downs). Do not refile CS-PF as this method.
tools_equipment: Named: hold-down anchors; 3x framing at tight edge nailing. Not a SKU list. Simpson holdowns are CLASS (c-P08-connector-class), no 2011 SKUs.

when_this_beats_habit: When BWL spacing, openings, wind, or SDC push the house out of IRC R602.10. PE path. Not because 8d@3 is tighter therefore better on a mild-climate house.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Copying the 160 mph WFCM example (hold-downs, 16 in practice, tight nailing) onto Wasatch/Fontana / low-wind IRC CS-WSP (D5). Using this as MF podium. Feeding Table 23 into a BWL house that still fits IRC.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They did not — it is a PE wall. Habit is BWL 6/12. Keep this method for when the house leaves the box.
permit_gate_notes: Engineer. Special inspector not named in these sources. Confirm with AHJ / engineer. No stamp from this KB.
risk_if_swapped_late: Dropping engineered shear back to IRC BWL after permit, or the reverse, changes hold-downs, 3x studs, and nail class. Catch before permit.
plain_language_summary: This is the engineer wall, not the usual house. Hold-downs at the ends, nails get tighter (6, then 4, then 3, then 2) as the load goes up, and 3x framing when you nail at 2 inches. Do not take a 160-mph workbook example and hang those hold-downs on a normal IRC house. Narrow garage portals in the code are CS-PF, not this.
spanish_summary: Esta es la pared del ingeniero, no la de siempre. Hold-downs en los extremos, clavos mas juntos (6, 4, 3, 2) segun la carga, y 3x cuando clava a 2 pulgadas. No copie el ejemplo de 160 mph y ponga esos anclajes en una casa IRC normal. El portal de cochera del codigo es CS-PF, no esto.
